items.guidance: What this site is: "warm, editorial, photography-led," or "dense, technical, mono-heavy," or "loud and cheap-feeling on purpose, because it's a discount tyre shop." Without this you get the default, and the default is what everyone else's AI-designed site looks like.

items.title: Typeface pair chosen and licence verified for commercial use
items.guidance: , including in a logo if it's going there. Open Font License and Google Fonts are safe; confirm rather than assume.

items.title: One distinctive element chosen
items.guidance: — the thing a visitor would describe to someone else afterwards. An oversized numeral, a duotone treatment, an unusual grid, a tracker rail. One. Sites without one are forgettable; sites with four are a mess.

items.title: Design brief written for the model and saved to the project
items.guidance: Art direction, the reference sites in the client's words, the real content, brand colours, audience, success measure. This is a project artifact now — it's what lets another agent pick up the work, and what lets you regenerate a page in a month without starting over.

items.title: Apple Developer Program enrolment started on day one
items.guidance: $99/year, client's account, client's card. An individual account is approved in days. An organization account needs a D-U-N-S number, which can take 1–2 weeks on its own, sometimes longer. If they want the company name on the listing, start this before you design anything.

items.title: Google Play Developer account created
items.guidance: $25 one-time, client's account. New personal developer accounts face additional testing requirements before public release — check the current rules and build the timeline around them rather than discovering them at submission.

items.guidance: The exact tasks, in order, with real examples of the inputs. Not "manage social media" — "at 9am, read the content calendar sheet, draft three posts in the brand voice, queue them for approval."

items.title: Every task sorted into one of three buckets
items.guidance: fully autonomous, needs approval before acting, or never automated. Written down and signed off.

items.title: Blast radius named for each autonomous task
items.guidance: If this runs wrong 100 times overnight, what's the worst outcome? Anything that can't be undone moves to the approval bucket.

items.title: Compliance reviewed for the specific use case
items.guidance: - Phone agents — call recording consent law varies by state and by the location of the person being called. Some states require all-party consent. Get the disclosure script written and approved before building anything. - Email — CAN-SPAM applies to bulk sending: real physical address, working unsubscribe. - Social — automated posting is against the terms of several platforms depending on how it's done. An account ban is a real outcome. Use official APIs and scheduling endpoints, never UI automation on a client's account.
